title: Aegis Users & Platform
_comment: Bump `version` on every edit — Grafana's file provisioner ignores a changed dashboard whose version did not increase.

list.name: price_starter
list.label: Starter $/mo
list.description: Plan prices live in Stripe, not in this repo — set your real ones here and the revenue panels follow.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) AS "users" FROM users

panels.title: Active now (15m)
panels.description: Access tokens are stateless, so there is no session to count. This is users who made an authenticated request in the last 15 minutes — the honest version of 'signed in right now'.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) AS "active" FROM users WHERE last_seen_at > now() - interval '15 minutes'
SELECT count(*) AS "active" FROM users WHERE last_seen_at > now() - interval '24 hours'
SELECT count(*) AS "active" FROM users WHERE last_seen_at > now() - interval '30 days'
SELECT count(*) AS "signups" FROM users WHERE created_at > now() - interval '7 days'

panels.title: Email verified
panels.description: Unverified accounts that never convert are the usual sign of a broken or spam-filtered verification mail.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE email_verified)::float / greatest(count(*), 1) AS "verified" FROM users
SELECT count(*) AS "paying" FROM users WHERE subscription_tier <> 'free' AND subscription_status IN ('active', 'trialing')
SELECT count(*) AS "deactivated" FROM users WHERE is_active = false

SELECT date_trunc('day', created_at) AS time, count(*) AS "signups"
FROM users
WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Daily active users
panels.description: Distinct people who did something auditable that day (created a scan, changed a member, issued a token). last_seen_at only holds the latest visit, so history comes from the audit log — this counts doers, not browsers.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT date_trunc('day', created_at) AS time, count(DISTINCT actor_user_id) AS "active users"
FROM audit_events
WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) AND actor_user_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

SELECT now() AS time, count(*) AS value, subscription_tier AS metric
FROM users
GROUP BY subscription_tier

SELECT now() AS time, count(*) AS value, subscription_status AS metric
FROM users
GROUP BY subscription_status

SELECT created_at AS "signed up", email, coalesce(display_name, '—') AS name,
       subscription_tier AS tier, email_verified AS verified, last_seen_at AS "last seen"
FROM users
ORDER BY created_at DESC
LIMIT 20

SELECT last_seen_at AS "last seen", email, subscription_tier AS tier,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM scans s WHERE s.created_by_user_id = u.id) AS scans
FROM users u
WHERE last_seen_at IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY last_seen_at DESC
LIMIT 20

panels.title: Activation rate
panels.description: Share of accounts that have ever started a scan. The single number that says whether signups turn into users.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT (SELECT count(DISTINCT created_by_user_id) FROM scans)::float
       / greatest((SELECT count(*) FROM users), 1) AS "activated"

panels.title: Accepted scan terms
panels.description: Scanning is gated on this attestation (see SECURITY.md), so it is also the last step before a user can do anything useful.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE scan_terms_accepted_at IS NOT NULL)::float / greatest(count(*), 1) AS "accepted" FROM users

panels.title: Signed up but never seen since
panels.description: Accounts older than a day with no authenticated request recorded. Dead signups.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) AS "dormant" FROM users WHERE last_seen_at IS NULL AND created_at < now() - interval '1 day'

SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE github_token IS NOT NULL OR gitlab_token IS NOT NULL OR bitbucket_token IS NOT NULL)::float
       / greatest(count(*), 1) AS "connected"
FROM users

SELECT date_trunc('day', created_at) AS time, count(*) AS value,
       coalesce(detail->>'method', 'unknown') AS metric
FROM audit_events
WHERE action = 'auth.login' AND $__timeFilter(created_at)
GROUP BY 1, 3
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Failed sign-ins per day
panels.description: A burst against one address, or from one IP, is what a takeover attempt looks like. 'inactive' means the password was right but the account is disabled.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT date_trunc('day', created_at) AS time, count(*) AS value,
       coalesce(detail->>'reason', 'unknown') AS metric
FROM audit_events
WHERE action = 'auth.login_failed' AND $__timeFilter(created_at)
GROUP BY 1, 3
ORDER BY 1
SELECT count(*) AS "failed" FROM audit_events WHERE action = 'auth.login_failed' AND created_at > now() - interval '24 hours'
SELECT count(*) AS "resets" FROM audit_events WHERE action = 'auth.password_reset' AND created_at > now() - interval '7 days'

panels.title: Addresses with the most failed attempts (7d)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT actor_email AS email,
       count(*) AS attempts,
       count(DISTINCT detail->>'ip') AS ips,
       max(created_at) AS "last attempt"
FROM audit_events
WHERE action = 'auth.login_failed' AND created_at > now() - interval '7 days'
GROUP BY actor_email
ORDER BY attempts DESC
LIMIT 20

SELECT created_at AS "when", action, actor_email AS email,
       detail->>'ip' AS ip,
       coalesce(detail->>'method', detail->>'reason', '') AS note
FROM audit_events
WHERE action LIKE 'auth.%'
ORDER BY created_at DESC
LIMIT 50
SELECT count(*) AS "orgs" FROM organizations

panels.title: Members per org (avg)
panels.description: Above 1 means the product is spreading inside a company rather than sitting with one person.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*)::float / greatest((SELECT count(*) FROM organizations), 1) AS "members" FROM org_memberships
SELECT count(*) AS "targets" FROM targets
SELECT count(*) AS "scans" FROM scans WHERE created_at > now() - interval '30 days'
SELECT count(*) AS "findings" FROM vulnerabilities WHERE created_at > now() - interval '30 days'

panels.title: LLM spend (30d)
panels.description: Cost of goods sold. Compare against what those users pay.

targets.rawSql: SELECT coalesce(sum(cost_usd), 0) AS "spend" FROM scans WHERE created_at > now() - interval '30 days'

SELECT date_trunc('day', created_at) AS time, count(*) AS value, status AS metric
FROM scans
WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at)
GROUP BY 1, 3
ORDER BY 1

SELECT date_trunc('day', created_at) AS time, count(*) AS value, severity AS metric
FROM vulnerabilities
WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at)
GROUP BY 1, 3
ORDER BY 1

SELECT date_trunc('day', created_at) AS time, coalesce(sum(cost_usd), 0) AS "cost"
FROM scans
WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Top organizations (30d)
panels.description: Who actually uses the platform, and what they cost to serve.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT o.name AS org,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM org_memberships m WHERE m.organization_id = o.id) AS members,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM targets t WHERE t.organization_id = o.id) AS targets,
       count(s.id) AS scans,
       coalesce(sum(s.cost_usd), 0) AS spend
FROM organizations o
LEFT JOIN targets t ON t.organization_id = o.id
LEFT JOIN scans s ON s.target_id = t.id AND s.created_at > now() - interval '30 days'
GROUP BY o.id, o.name
ORDER BY scans DESC, spend DESC
LIMIT 20

panels.title: Activation funnel
panels.description: Every stage is measured against all accounts ever created, so this is lifetime reach per step, not a per-cohort conversion. Scans started with an API token have no user attached and do not count toward the last two stages.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT s.stage, s.users
FROM (VALUES
  (1, 'signed up',      (SELECT count(*) FROM users)),
  (2, 'verified email', (SELECT count(*) FROM users WHERE email_verified)),
  (3, 'accepted terms', (SELECT count(*) FROM users WHERE scan_terms_accepted_at IS NOT NULL)),
  (4, 'connected git',  (SELECT count(*) FROM users WHERE github_token IS NOT NULL OR gitlab_token IS NOT NULL OR bitbucket_token IS NOT NULL)),
  (5, 'added a target', (SELECT count(DISTINCT created_by_user_id) FROM targets)),
  (6, 'ran a scan',     (SELECT count(DISTINCT created_by_user_id) FROM scans)),
  (7, 'ran 2+ scans',   (SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT created_by_user_id FROM scans WHERE created_by_user_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*) > 1) m))
) AS s(ord, stage, users)
ORDER BY s.ord

panels.title: Where signups fall out
panels.description: The largest 'lost here' is the one worth fixing first.

targets.rawSql:
WITH t AS (SELECT greatest(count(*), 1)::float AS total FROM users)
SELECT s.stage, s.users,
       s.users / t.total AS "of signups",
       1 - s.users::float / nullif(lag(s.users) OVER (ORDER BY s.ord), 0) AS "lost here"
FROM t, (VALUES
  (1, 'signed up',      (SELECT count(*) FROM users)),
  (2, 'verified email', (SELECT count(*) FROM users WHERE email_verified)),
  (3, 'accepted terms', (SELECT count(*) FROM users WHERE scan_terms_accepted_at IS NOT NULL)),
  (4, 'connected git',  (SELECT count(*) FROM users WHERE github_token IS NOT NULL OR gitlab_token IS NOT NULL OR bitbucket_token IS NOT NULL)),
  (5, 'added a target', (SELECT count(DISTINCT created_by_user_id) FROM targets)),
  (6, 'ran a scan',     (SELECT count(DISTINCT created_by_user_id) FROM scans)),
  (7, 'ran 2+ scans',   (SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT created_by_user_id FROM scans WHERE created_by_user_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*) > 1) m))
) AS s(ord, stage, users)
ORDER BY s.ord

panels.title: Weekly retention cohorts
panels.description: Each row is the week a set of accounts signed up; W0..W7 is the share of that cohort seen doing something in the audit log that many weeks later. Sign-ins are audited from 0016 onward — cohorts older than that only show people who changed something, so early rows read low.

targets.rawSql:
WITH c AS (
  SELECT id, date_trunc('week', created_at) AS cohort_week FROM users
),
a AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT c.id, c.cohort_week,
         (floor(extract(epoch FROM date_trunc('week', e.created_at) - c.cohort_week) / 604800))::int AS wk
  FROM c
  JOIN audit_events e ON e.actor_user_id = c.id
)
SELECT to_char(c.cohort_week, 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS cohort,
       count(DISTINCT c.id) AS signups,
       count(DISTINCT a.id) FILTER (WHERE a.wk = 0)::float / count(DISTINCT c.id) AS "W0",
       count(DISTINCT a.id) FILTER (WHERE a.wk = 1)::float / count(DISTINCT c.id) AS "W1",
       count(DISTINCT a.id) FILTER (WHERE a.wk = 2)::float / count(DISTINCT c.id) AS "W2",
       count(DISTINCT a.id) FILTER (WHERE a.wk = 3)::float / count(DISTINCT c.id) AS "W3",
       count(DISTINCT a.id) FILTER (WHERE a.wk = 4)::float / count(DISTINCT c.id) AS "W4",
       count(DISTINCT a.id) FILTER (WHERE a.wk = 5)::float / count(DISTINCT c.id) AS "W5",
       count(DISTINCT a.id) FILTER (WHERE a.wk = 6)::float / count(DISTINCT c.id) AS "W6",
       count(DISTINCT a.id) FILTER (WHERE a.wk = 7)::float / count(DISTINCT c.id) AS "W7"
FROM c
LEFT JOIN a ON a.id = c.id
GROUP BY c.cohort_week
ORDER BY c.cohort_week DESC
LIMIT 12

panels.title: MRR
panels.description: Subscribed accounts priced at the rates set in the dashboard variables above. Trialing accounts are counted — they are revenue you are about to have or about to lose.

panels.title: LLM cost (30d)
panels.description: What the scans actually cost to run. Only scans that recorded a cost count.

targets.rawSql: SELECT coalesce(sum(cost_usd), 0) AS "llm cost" FROM scans WHERE created_at > now() - interval '30 days'

panels.title: Gross margin
panels.description: One month of revenue against one month of LLM spend. Ignores infrastructure, salaries and Stripe's cut — it is the engine's margin, not the company's.

panels.title: Underwater orgs
panels.description: Organizations whose scans cost more in the last 30 days than their owner's plan brings in. A free-tier org that somehow ran scans lands here too.

targets.rawSql:
WITH o AS (
  SELECT org.id, CASE WHEN u.subscription_status IN ('active', 'trialing')
            THEN CASE u.subscription_tier
                   WHEN 'starter' THEN ${price_starter}
                   WHEN 'pro' THEN ${price_pro}
                   WHEN 'enterprise' THEN ${price_enterprise}
                   ELSE 0 END
            ELSE 0 END::numeric AS price
  FROM organizations org JOIN users u ON u.id = org.owner_user_id
)
SELECT count(*) AS "underwater" FROM (
  SELECT o.id, o.price - coalesce(sum(s.cost_usd), 0)::numeric AS margin
  FROM o
  LEFT JOIN targets t ON t.organization_id = o.id
  LEFT JOIN scans s ON s.target_id = t.id AND s.created_at > now() - interval '30 days'
  GROUP BY o.id, o.price
) m WHERE margin < 0

panels.title: Per-organization economics (30d)
panels.description: Worst margin first. Revenue is the owner's plan price; cost is every scan run against that org's targets.

targets.rawSql:
WITH o AS (
  SELECT org.id, org.name, u.email AS owner, u.subscription_tier AS tier,
         CASE WHEN u.subscription_status IN ('active', 'trialing')
            THEN CASE u.subscription_tier
                   WHEN 'starter' THEN ${price_starter}
                   WHEN 'pro' THEN ${price_pro}
                   WHEN 'enterprise' THEN ${price_enterprise}
                   ELSE 0 END
            ELSE 0 END::numeric AS price
  FROM organizations org JOIN users u ON u.id = org.owner_user_id
)
SELECT o.name AS org, o.owner, o.tier,
       o.price AS "revenue/mo",
       count(s.id) AS "scans 30d",
       coalesce(sum(s.cost_usd), 0)::numeric AS "llm cost 30d",
       o.price - coalesce(sum(s.cost_usd), 0)::numeric AS "margin"
FROM o
LEFT JOIN targets t ON t.organization_id = o.id
LEFT JOIN scans s ON s.target_id = t.id AND s.created_at > now() - interval '30 days'
GROUP BY o.id, o.name, o.owner, o.tier, o.price
ORDER BY "margin" ASC
LIMIT 20
